decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach with both grippers open; cameras will go in center basket, figures left, pens right. Establish downward approach gradually.
Approach the two cameras from above in separate workspaces, increasing downward tilt without changing elbow branch.
Fine-align over each camera and descend cautiously; wrist views will determine final grasp adjustment.
Center the cameras between the jaws, close gradually, and make a small test lift to check retention in RGB.
Lift both cameras clear and advance the right camera toward the center basket first, keeping the left arm separated and stationary after lifting.
Right camera remains retained; lower it over the center basket. Left camera slipped onto the table, so reopen and reorient for a width-wise grasp.
Replan after continuity guard: lower the right wrist and pitch forward to reach inside the basket without further extension; continue left camera alignment.
Release right camera into blue basket and clear it. Finish aligning left jaws across the camera's narrow dimension before closing.
Test-lift and transport the left camera, keeping its jaws closed. Move the right arm outward to approach the white pen across its short dimension.
Bring the retained left camera above blue basket while keeping arms apart. Rotate the right jaws to align across the white pen, close, and test retention.
Open left gripper and clear the blue basket to inspect the camera's landing; retention appears uncertain. Lift the white pen and start its transfer toward red.
Both recent grasps failed visually. Reapproach the fallen camera and white pen with open jaws, more vertical alignment, and a lower grasp depth.
Close and test-lift the aligned white pen. Narrow left opening to clear the adjacent basket rim, adjust leftward, and descend for the camera grasp.
White pen is retained; carry it toward the red basket. Left camera remains on the table: advance slightly and lower with a narrowed opening, checking possible rim interference.
Release the retained pen into red, then clear it. Use wrist-image alignment to shift left jaws toward the camera rather than the adjacent rim, close and test-lift.
Pen is visibly in red. Camera is now centered in left wrist view but grasp was above its sides; reopen, descend another 3 cm and close.
Camera now lies between the left finger pads. Lift vertically to verify retention, then begin a short transfer toward blue while the right arm stays clear.
Camera slipped again. Reorient to a truly vertical grasp across its short axis, then approach its observed location with open jaws.
The basket rim blocks the left descent. Move left of the rim first, narrow the opening, and approach the exposed side of the camera.
Camera is now visually between the left finger pads. Close without translating, then perform only a small vertical retention test.
The camera remained on the table. Shift the wrist toward its image center and descend with open jaws so the pads engage below its top surface.
Close on the camera's sides at the improved wrist alignment, pause, then make a short vertical test lift.
Head view shows the fingers left of the camera, despite wrist-image overlap. Correct rightward within the left workspace and grasp its rear side away from the basket rim.
Lift slowly with the camera clamped, then make a small motion toward blue; verify the camera moves with the fingers before committing to placement.
Change the left grasp direction so the open fingers stay parallel to the basket's front rim rather than striking it; maintain clearance during reorientation.
Descend vertically toward the camera with jaws aligned along the basket front, avoiding the previously obstructing rim.
Close at the unobstructed lower pose and perform a short vertical test lift while watching the camera in the head view.
Camera is visibly retained after the test lift. Lift clear of the rim and pitch it forward over the left half of blue while maintaining a closed grasp.
The camera slipped during transfer and is now clear of the rim. Reapproach its new location vertically, aiming for a deeper side grasp before lifting.
Lower the camera grasp another 18 mm with a small centering correction; close and pause at depth before any transport.
Lift the camera vertically with unchanged orientation and closed jaws, avoiding the rotation that previously caused slipping.
Camera remains retained. Gain rim clearance, then translate toward blue without rotating the grasp.
Continuity guard prevents further high forward reach. Lower and gently pitch the retained camera into blue instead, keeping the grasp closed.
Release the second camera into blue, allow it to settle, and approach the gray figure with the left arm for the white basket.
Center the left pads around the gray figure's torso, descend to its sides, and close before testing retention.
Test-lift the gray figure with unchanged orientation, then begin moving left toward the white basket if retained.
Gray figure slipped and rotated upright. Recenter on its lower torso and grasp more deeply with open pads before closing.
The figure is lying on the table; the last closure was above its sides. Reopen and lower to a table-level torso grasp before closing.
Lift the torso grasp without rotating, then translate left toward the white basket. Verify the figure stays fixed between the pads.
Carry the retained gray figure toward white, raising and pitching gradually to keep its feet above the rim while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Move the retained figure fully past the white basket's front rim, lower slightly, and release into the interior.
Gray figure is inside white. Approach the remaining blue-clothed figure with the left gripper; stage the right arm on its own side for the later pen transfer.
Descend to the blue figure's torso at the successful lower grasp depth, rotating the open jaws to match its diagonal body.
Wrist view shows the jaws over the head rather than the torso. Shift toward the blue clothing, slightly lower, then close around the body.
Test-lift the blue figure with the closed grasp and unchanged orientation, then begin the short transfer toward white.
Blue figure remains fixed in the grasp. Carry it over white with gradual forward pitch and rim clearance, keeping the right arm separated.
Lower the retained blue figure fully inside white, open the gripper, and lift clear to inspect the category basket.
Both figures are in white and both cameras in blue. Approach the remaining left pen from above; it will be staged at center for the right arm to place in red.
Align the left jaws across the remaining pen and descend to table-level grasp depth while keeping the right arm clear.
Correct the pen's lateral offset in the wrist view, lower slightly, then close with the jaws across the barrel.
Lift the pen and begin moving toward a central staging location, preserving the grasp and keeping the right arm clear.
Carry the retained pen toward center for staging, with the left wrist remaining on its own side. Move the right arm outward for safe separation.
Lower the pen onto the center table and open the left gripper. Its right-hand end will be accessible to the right arm without crossing.
Correct the rejected tensor; no previous motion executed. Clear the left arm up and left while approaching the staged pen's right end at height with the right arm.
Approach the pen's right-side barrel with open right jaws and descend to grasp depth. Retract and gradually unpitch the empty left arm toward its origin.
Fine-center the right jaws across the pen barrel and close at depth. Continue the empty left arm's gradual return near its origin.
Test-lift the staged pen vertically with the right grasp closed. Complete the empty left arm's small remaining return to origin.
Pen remained on the table after lifting. Reopen, correct toward its right-side barrel in the head view, and approach slightly deeper before closing again.
Remove the slight wrist roll and table interference, recenter the pen between the right pads, then close at a level grasp pose.
Test-lift the centered pen with unchanged wrist orientation and closed jaws, then begin a small rightward transfer.
The pen is visibly retained. Transport it across the right workspace toward red, keeping the wrist orientation and closed grasp unchanged.
Advance the retained pen over red with gentle forward pitch and rim clearance, positioning its full length within that basket.
The pen slipped during the pitched transfer and is on the table in front of red. Reapproach its middle with a level wrist and limited opening to avoid the rim.
The pen was nudged away from the rim and is now accessible. Recenter over its middle at the new position, align the jaws, and close at table depth.
Lift without rotation to check whether the pen is retained and clear the rim contact, then withdraw slightly before replanning.
The pen remains on the table. Align across its new diagonal orientation, shift onto the central barrel, and descend with a rim-safe opening.
Make a small lateral wrist correction onto the pen, close at the barrel, and test retention with a short vertical lift.
Lift the newly centered pen well above the red rim with no wrist rotation, checking that it stays fixed between the pads.
Pen stays fixed in the grasp. Translate straight forward over red without rotating, maintaining clearance for the entire pen.
The pen is fully over red. After the continuity guard, lower instead of reaching farther, then open and let it settle inside.
All six objects are visibly in their category baskets. Clear the right gripper above the rim, then retract and begin returning its orientation toward origin.
Both pens are settled in red. Retract the empty right arm toward its origin with gradual unrotation, preserving the elbow-up branch.
Complete the right arm's return to its starting pose with both grippers open; the objects remain separated in their three baskets.
